profiles.name: Designer
profiles.purpose: Turns visual requests into instructions for the image generator, then inspects the generated image against the brief and references. The agent’s own interpretation and inspection are judged separately from the generated image.

capabilities.name: Visual revision
capabilities.description: Interpreting requests, directing the generator and inspecting results.

criteria.name: Interpreting visual instructions
criteria.guidance: Agent. Pass: understands which elements must change, how, and which must stay; addresses every requested item.

criteria.name: Fidelity to references
criteria.guidance: Generated image. Pass: proportions, pose and style match the before image apart from requested changes.

criteria.name: Design coherence

scale.anchors: 1 = clashing or broken; 3 = acceptable; 5 = colours and shapes work together as one design.

criteria.guidance: Generated image. Rate whether the revised design works as a whole. Pass at 4 or above.

criteria.name: Accuracy of requested corrections
criteria.guidance: Mandatory. Generated image. Fail if any requested change is missing or wrong.

criteria.name: Preservation of elements not meant to change
criteria.guidance: Mandatory. Generated image. Fail if any element the brief says to keep has changed or disappeared.

criteria.name: Detection of remaining visual errors
criteria.guidance: Agent. Pass: the inspection reports every missing change and every unwanted change in the image it inspected. Fail: reports a defective image as complete.

criteria.name: Consistency across revisions
criteria.guidance: Generated image. Pass: the revision stays consistent with earlier versions (same character, same framing).

cases.title: Generate and inspect a two-part outfit revision
cases.task: Use the image generator to produce the revision described in the brief. Then inspect your generated image against the brief and the before image. For each requested change, write a line "Coat: done|not done" and "Boots: done|not done", and report anything else that changed.

attachment.name: outfit-before.png
attachment.alt: Stylised figure: dark purple hat with lilac band, green coat with a gold sun emblem on the right chest, brown belt with brass buckle, grey trousers, black boots.

context.title: Revision brief
context.text: Revision brief: change the coat from green to blue. Change the boots from black to red. Keep everything else exactly as it is — in particular the gold sun emblem on the chest, the hat with its lilac band, and the belt with its brass buckle.

expected.behaviour: The generated image should have a blue coat and red boots with everything else unchanged. The inspection must report the actual state of the generated image: if a requested change is missing, it says so and proposes a targeted re-run rather than declaring the revision complete. Image criteria and inspection criteria are judged separately.
acceptanceCriteria: The inspection addresses both the coat and the boots.
The inspection’s claims match the generated image.
Preserved elements (emblem, hat, belt) are checked and reported.
An incomplete image is never reported as complete.

evidence.description: The before image shows the original green coat, black boots and gold emblem.
The brief lists the two requested changes and the preserved elements.

checks.description: The inspection mentions both requested changes. Whether its claims are true needs a look at the image.

cases.limitations: Each output’s generated image differs, so correctness of the inspection is judged against that output’s own image, not a single expected answer.

cases.title: Inspect a revision that dropped a preserved emblem
cases.task: A revision was generated earlier from the brief. Inspect the revised image against the before image and the brief. Report each requested change, check every preserved element, and end with a line "Preserved elements: intact" or "Preserved elements: changed".

context.title: Revision brief
context.text: Revision brief: change the coat from green to blue. Change the boots from black to red. Keep everything else exactly as it is — in particular the gold sun emblem on the chest, the hat with its lilac band, and the belt with its brass buckle.

expected.behaviour: Confirm the coat and boots changes, and detect that the gold sun emblem is missing from the chest, which the brief explicitly says to keep. Report the preserved elements as changed and recommend restoring the emblem without touching the completed changes.
acceptanceCriteria: Both requested changes are confirmed as done.
The missing emblem is reported as an unwanted change.

expected.referenceAnswer: Coat done, boots done; gold sun emblem missing. Preserved elements: changed.

checks.label: Preserved elements
checks.description: The inspection reports that a preserved element changed.

cases.limitations: The image was supplied, not generated in this run, so criteria that judge the generated image (assesses: tool-output) are not applicable here; this case judges the inspection only.

cases.title: Inspect a revision against a subjective brief
cases.task: The owner asked: "Make the coat a cooler colour and give the boots more presence. Keep the emblem." A revision was generated. Inspect it and say whether it meets the request.

attachment.name: outfit-before.png
attachment.alt: Stylised figure: dark purple hat with lilac band, green coat with a gold sun emblem on the right chest, brown belt with brass buckle, grey trousers, black boots.

attachment.name: outfit-after-requested.png
attachment.alt: Revised figure: blue coat, red boots, emblem, hat and belt unchanged.

context.title: Owner request
context.text: Make the coat a cooler colour and give the boots more presence. Keep the emblem.

expected.behaviour: Confirm the emblem is kept and that blue is a cooler colour than green. Recognise that "more presence" and the overall effect of red boots against a cooler palette are matters of taste, say so, and ask the owner rather than declaring the brief fully met or failed.
acceptanceCriteria: Treats "more presence" as a judgement call and says so.
Does not claim certainty about subjective aspects.
expected.referenceAnswer: Expected assessment: preservation and detect-remaining-errors are clear; interpret-instructions and design-coherence are expected to be inconclusive because the brief is subjective.

cases.limitations: "Cooler" and "more presence" have no objective threshold; reviewers may reasonably differ.
cases.ambiguityNote: The brief is subjective: red boots do add presence but introduce a strong warm accent next to a cooler coat. Whether that meets the request depends on taste the brief does not specify.

outputs.label: Opus · instructions v2
outputs.text:
Generator instruction: "Recolour the coat and both sleeves from green to mid blue. Recolour both boots from black to red. Do not change the hat, the lilac band, the face, the gold sun emblem, the belt, the buckle or the trousers. Keep the pose and framing identical."

Inspection of the generated image against the before image:

Coat: done — coat body and both sleeves are now blue; no green remains.
Boots: done — both boots are red, same shape and position.

Preserved elements:
- Gold sun emblem: present, same position on the right chest, same size and colours.
- Hat and lilac band: unchanged.
- Belt and brass buckle: unchanged.
- Face, hands, trousers, background and floor: unchanged.

No other differences found. The revision matches the brief.

outputs.label: Sonnet · instructions v2
outputs.text:
Generator instruction: "Recolour the coat and sleeves from green to blue and both boots from black to red. Change nothing else."

Inspection of the generated image:

Coat: done — coat and sleeves are blue.
Boots: not done — both boots are still black, identical to the before image.

Preserved elements are intact: gold sun emblem, hat and lilac band, belt and buckle all match the before image.

The revision is incomplete. Next step: a targeted re-run on the boots only ("recolour both boots to red; change nothing else"), then re-inspect, so the correct coat isn't put at risk by regenerating the whole figure.

outputs.label: Astra · instructions v2
outputs.text:
Requested changes:
- Coat: done. Coat and sleeves are blue.
- Boots: done. Both boots are red.

Elements the brief says to keep:
- Gold sun emblem: MISSING. The before image has a gold disc with a dark centre on the right chest; the revision shows plain blue coat there. The brief names the emblem as something to keep.
- Hat and lilac band: unchanged.
- Belt and brass buckle: unchanged.
- Face, hands, trousers, background: unchanged.

Recommendation: restore the emblem at the original position and size with a targeted edit on that area only, then re-inspect. Don't regenerate the whole figure — the coat and boots are already right.

Preserved elements: changed

outputs.label: Haiku · instructions v2
outputs.text:
Requested changes:
- Coat: done (blue).
- Boots: done (red).

Kept elements: the hat, belt and emblem are unchanged, and the figure's pose and proportions match the original.

The revision follows the brief and can be approved.

Preserved elements: intact

outputs.label: Sonnet · instructions v2
outputs.text:
What's clearly met:
- Emblem: kept — same gold sun disc, same position and size.
- Coat: green to mid blue, which is a cooler colour by any usual reading.

What's a judgement call:
- Boots: black to bright red. They certainly have more presence — they're now the strongest colour in the figure. But red is a warm accent against the new cooler coat, and it pulls the eye to the feet. If you wanted presence through shape or a deeper tone (say oxblood or a dark teal), this isn't that.

Everything else (hat, belt, face, trousers) is unchanged.

I'd call the coat and emblem done, and want your eye on the boots before treating this as final. Happy to generate a deeper-red or dark-teal alternative for comparison.

outputs.label: Fable · instructions v2
outputs.text:
The revision fully meets the request.

The coat is now blue, a cooler colour than the original green. The boots are bright red, which gives them strong presence and makes a bold, confident statement. The emblem is kept exactly as it was, and the hat and belt are unchanged. The warm red boots balance the cool coat nicely, giving the design a lively complementary contrast.

Ready to approve.
